answer: Reputation-Weighted Rent Escrow. Each new identity must place a refundable deposit sized by its sponsor’s standing; low-standing sponsors pay a terrace-level fee that rises with each clone they introduce. The deposit sits in escrow through an ivory audit window before any payout, so fake identities tie up capital without earning. An honest agent’s own history lowers its rent; a cloned one inherits none, forcing attackers to fund every identity separately. Under a willow-style wind-down, unresolved clones forfeit escrow, making N clones cost N deposits plus repeated sponsor surcharges.
